title: Destroying a child navigable should detach its subtree synchronously
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

See:

```html
<iframe id=f srcdoc="<iframe></iframe>"></iframe>
<script>
  const w = f.contentWindow;
  f.remove();
  console.log(w.length); // Should be 0, is 1 per spec
</script>
```

With current spec, it should log "1", but all browsers and WPT log "0".

1. `remove()` runs [destroy a child navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#destroy-a-child-navigable).
2. Step 5 calls [destroy a document and its descendants](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-lifecycle.html#destroy-a-document-and-its-descendants), which begins "perform the following steps in parallel".
3. `w.length` ends up calling [document-tree child navigables](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#document-tree-child-navigables). Step 1 return if the document's [node navigable](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/document-sequences.html#node-navigable) is null, but that unloading is happening in parallel, so the length is still "1"

While parts of unloading does need to happen in parallel by necessity for cross site frames, the above shows that at least some parts of this algorithm will need to run synchronously
